sources.title: Wikipedia, "Counterpoint"
sources.supports: Two or more simultaneous lines that are harmonically dependent but rhythmically independent; imitative counterpoint repeats a main idea across voices; parallel voices are prohibited because they destroy voice independence

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Fugue"
sources.supports: Subject stated in imitation at different pitches, exposition complete when every voice has entered, episodes between entries, entries in related keys, final entry in the tonic; Bach as the model

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Ornament (music)"
sources.supports: Trill as rapid alternation between a note and the one above it, mordent as a single quick alternation, ornaments improvised in the Baroque and expected from a keyboard player

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Circle of fifths"
sources.supports: The twelve pitch classes in ascending fifths; chord progressions often move between roots a fifth apart, and modulation goes to a key one signature away

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Ostinato" (ground bass redirects here)
sources.supports: A figure that persistently repeats in the same voice, exact repetition or repetition with variation, and the ground bass as a bass line repeated under changing upper parts

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Sequence (music)"
sources.supports: Restatement of a motif at a higher or lower pitch in the same voice, usually two to four segments in one direction at the same interval distance, real versus tonal sequences

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Alberti bass"
sources.supports: Broken chord accompaniment presenting the chord as lowest, highest, middle, highest, repeated, typical of the Classical era; named after Domenico Alberti

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Cadence"
sources.supports: The four cadence types with their chord motions: authentic V to I or V7 to I, half ending on V, plagal IV to I, deceptive V to vi; a ii-V-I example in C major; the cadence as the cradle of tonality

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Sonata form"
sources.supports: Exposition, development and recapitulation as the three large sections, with introduction and coda optional

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Rondo"
sources.supports: A refrain alternating with contrasting episodes, the patterns ABACA and ABACABA named, and the form as the height of its popularity in the late eighteenth century

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Minuet"
sources.supports: A dance usually in 3/4; the early minuet usually binary with two repeated sections of about eight bars, later a rounded binary A B A with the trio in the middle

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Period (music)"
sources.supports: A period as an antecedent plus a consequent phrase, about eight bars, the antecedent ending in a weaker cadence (often half) and the consequent in a stronger one (often authentic)

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Power chord"
sources.supports: A power chord is the root plus the fifth and possibly octaves, with no third, so it is neither major nor minor; the 3:2 ratio keeps it coherent under distortion; it survives fast chord changes

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Palm mute"
sources.supports: Damping the strings at the bridge while picking gives the short chugging attack; heavier muting shortens the note and adds percussion; thrash metal fused it with fast alternate picking

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Alternate picking" (tremolo picking redirects here)
sources.supports: Rapid down and up strokes on one note at high speed are called tremolo; alternate picking is required at very high tempos; palm muting plus alternate picking gives blast picking, the machine gun riff of thrash and death metal

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Phrygian dominant scale"
sources.supports: Phrygian dominant as the fifth mode of harmonic minor, spelled 1 b2 3 4 5 b6 b7, its flat second and augmented second as the signature intervals, its main chords I, bII, iv and vii, and its use for secondary dominants

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Pentatonic scale"
sources.supports: The minor pentatonic as scale degrees 1, b3, 4, 5 and b7 of the natural minor, described as a gapped blues scale, with no semitones in the anhemitonic form

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Dorian mode"
sources.supports: Dorian as a diatonic mode with a major sixth; the i to III to VII to IV chord sequence that reads as minor but ends with a major third above the tonic

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Chiptune"
sources.supports: With few voices the standard way to fake polyphony is a quick arpeggio, described as one of the most relevant features of chip music

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Harmonic minor scale"
sources.supports: The raised seventh makes an augmented second between the sixth and seventh degrees; harmonically it is used over V7 rather than over the tonic; the diminished triad on the raised seventh has dominant function; the scale spawned neoclassical metal

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Phrase (music)"
sources.supports: A phrase ends with a cadence; in common practice phrases are often four bars, and the antecedent and consequent are the two halves of a period

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Nintendocore"
sources.supports: A style fusing chiptune and game music with hardcore punk and heavy metal; bands such as Minibosses play NES repertoire with heavy metal riffing, which shows the repertoire carries rock and metal reading

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Mega Man 2"

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Castlevania"

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Contra (video game)"

sources.title: Wikipedia, "Bass drum" (double bass drum redirects here)

recipes.name: Prelude harp arpeggio
recipes.rule: Play the chord as an up then down broken chord over two octaves in sixteenths on pulse1, and repeat the same figure on pulse2 one eighth later at lower volume, so the pair reads as a harp with a delay
recipes.params_text: subdivision=16ths; octaves=2; order=up_then_down; notes=chord_tones_only; delay_eighths=1; vol_pct=40; channel=pulse1+pulse2

recipes.name: Detuned shimmer pair
recipes.rule: Play one melody on two pulses at the same rhythm, the second pulse shifted a few cents flat and a fraction later, which is the trick that makes plain square tones feel emotional

recipes.name: Maiden arpeggio and melody
recipes.rule: Under a delicate single line melody, let a simple arpeggio of the chord run in eighths on pulse1 with the melody on vrc6_p1, keeping the arpeggio below the melody in register

recipes.name: Driving sixteenth battle riff
recipes.rule: Play a repeating sixteenth riff on pulse1 at a fixed two bar cell, put the root on the triangle on every beat, and put a noise hit on beats 2 and 4

recipes.name: Baroque fanfare cadence
recipes.rule: End a cue with a rising arpeggio figure on pulse1, a sawtooth chord stab on vrc6_saw, then a single held tonic, in a shape that arrives at the last bar

recipes.name: Ostinato under arpeggio
recipes.rule: Hold a repeated root and fifth ostinato on the triangle under the UEM-01 arpeggio, so the harmony is stated twice by two different voices

recipes.name: Three note melody discipline
recipes.rule: Write the lead melody for one pulse channel only and put no more than three distinct pitches in any two bar span, because the NES cannot play three notes at once and Mother was written inside that limit

recipes.name: Jazz town shuffle
recipes.rule: Write a town cue with a swung eighth feel over a walking triangle bass, and give the melody a blue third, because EarthBound deliberately carried more jazzy pieces than Mother

recipes.name: Slow vibrato on held notes
recipes.rule: Bend the pitch of any melody note held longer than a quarter note by a few cents and back, the string bending that EarthBound is credited with bringing to a video game

recipes.name: Bicycle lilt
recipes.rule: Write a travel cue in a compound feel with a skipping melody in thirds, a light triangle accompaniment on beats 1 and 3, and no drum layer at all

recipes.name: Style switch per place
recipes.rule: Give each location its own style and its own rhythmic signature, and let the piece change style between locations rather than varying one global theme

recipes.name: Music and effects as one
recipes.rule: Use the noise channel as part of the arrangement, not only as a separate effect layer, so that the track and the sound effects share one surface

recipes.name: One finger singable theme
recipes.rule: Write the theme as a single line, stepwise, with no leap larger than a fourth and no more than one chromatic note in the whole phrase, so that a beginner can play it with one finger and hum it

recipes.name: Layered hidden motif
recipes.rule: Keep one secondary motif in reserve and reveal it only in the secret or late scene, so the earlier scenes feel like they were hiding something

recipes.name: Recast the leitmotif
recipes.rule: Reuse the same melodic cell in a new scene and change only the instrumentation and the register, never the notes, so the listener recognises the place from the melody

recipes.name: Adaptive instrument on a state flag
recipes.rule: Bind the instrument of the current cue to a game state flag, so the same cue plays as a different instrument when the state changes, as the music box variant does

recipes.name: Music first, scene second
recipes.rule: Write the cue before the scene it belongs to, then name the scene in the cue metadata, so the music sets the emotion the scene then has to carry

recipes.name: Simple line that grows
recipes.rule: Keep the melody inside a narrow range with one deliberate deviation, then let the arrangement grow around it without changing the melody

recipes.name: Character theme with a signature rhythm
recipes.rule: Give each character theme one rhythmic signature, a fixed two or three note figure that carries the personality, and keep the drum pattern behind it constant and driving

recipes.name: Field then town, same melody
recipes.rule: Write a sparse field cue with a small instrumental palette, then write the town cue as the same melody with more voices and a brighter rhythm

recipes.name: Small synth set for the whole score
recipes.rule: Restrict the whole score to one small set of soundfonts and synths and reuse them everywhere, as the 2015 2D RPG score does with its soundfonts

recipes.name: Duty layering for melody and accompaniment
recipes.rule: Give the lead a 12.5 or 25 percent duty pulse and the accompaniment a 50 percent duty pulse, so the two voices stay separable under the mixer

recipes.name: Triangle bass with envelope bass
recipes.rule: Put the bass line on the triangle and vary its loudness with the sweep unit falling in pitch on each note, which is the classic NES bass envelope

recipes.name: Noise kit from the LFSR rates
recipes.rule: Build the percussion kit from the noise channel only: a short high rate burst for the hat, a mid rate burst for the snare, and a periodic mode burst for a metallic hit

recipes.name: DPCM kick
recipes.rule: Use the sample channel for a kick drum, because a one bit sample gives a pitched thump that the noise channel cannot, and keep the sample short

recipes.name: Sawtooth pad and oom pah
recipes.rule: Use the VRC6 sawtooth as a sustained pad on long values and as an oom pah two hit stab on beats 2 and 3 of a waltz, with a rate that stays under the distortion threshold

recipes.name: VRC6 pulse doubling and echo
recipes.rule: Double the lead with the second VRC6 pulse a step below, or use the VRC6 pulse in 100 percent mode as a flat organ voice for a held chord

recipes.name: Falling sweep line
recipes.rule: Express a falling melody line by enabling the sweep unit with the negate flag so the pitch glides down under each note

recipes.name: Delayed echo voice
recipes.rule: Send a copy of the lead to the second pulse one eighth later at reduced volume, the way the FF I Prelude does, and vary the delay across sections

recipes.name: Instantiate a mood grammar
recipes.rule: Pick the grammar for the mood of the scene from section 7, draw the progression for the key of the cue, and drop the section that does not fit the scene's function

recipes.name: Two voice imitative entry
recipes.rule: State the subject on pulse1, bring pulse2 in on the same subject one bar later at the fifth above, and give pulse1 free eighths from that point so the two voices never move in the same rhythm

recipes.name: Four entry exposition
recipes.rule: Alternate subject and answer on the two pulses for four entries, with a two bar episode between entries, and drop the entry that would collide rather than voice crossing

recipes.name: Tonal sequence
recipes.rule: Restate a two beat motif at the next scale step, three segments in one direction, then cadence; use diatonic transposition so the sequence stays in key

recipes.name: Circle of fifths descent
recipes.rule: Move the roots down a fifth every bar for four bars and put the function order pre-dominant to dominant to tonic at the end of the chain, with the root on the triangle and the chord broken on pulse2

recipes.name: Ground bass
recipes.rule: Repeat one four bar triangle figure exactly two to four times and change only the pulse parts above it, so the bass is the fixed point and the melody is the argument

recipes.name: Trill on a long note
recipes.rule: When a melody note is a quarter or longer, alternate it with the upper diatonic neighbour in 32nds for the last third of its value, on 12.5 percent duty so the two pitches stay distinct

recipes.name: Mordent on an accent
recipes.rule: Start an accented note with three quick notes main, lower neighbour, main at 64th rate, which costs two frames and marks the beat

recipes.name: Arpeggiated chord figure
recipes.rule: Break the chord root, third, fifth, octave upward in sixteenths over two octaves on pulse2, which is the chip's only way to state a triad and the Baroque way to state it too

recipes.name: Dance pair, binary
recipes.rule: Write section A of 8 bars in the tonic and section B of 8 bars starting on the dominant, repeat both, and keep one rhythmic figure for the whole dance

recipes.name: Cadential trill to the tonic
recipes.rule: Put the trill on the penultimate note of the phrase and land the tonic on the last beat, with the bass moving fifth to first under it, so the ornament and the cadence are one gesture

recipes.name: Cantus firmus against motion
recipes.rule: Hold long values on pulse2 (halves and wholes) while pulse1 moves in eighths, forbid voice crossing, and let the slow voice change only on strong beats so the motion is audibly one voice

recipes.name: Organ chorale stab
recipes.rule: Use the first VRC6 pulse in 100 percent duty as a held chorale voice, move one voice at a time, and double the bass on the triangle so the four voice texture reads as four voices on seven channels

recipes.name: Alberti bass
recipes.rule: Under the melody, break the chord on pulse2 in the order lowest, highest, middle, highest at eighth rate, one chord per bar, which is the standard Classical accompaniment and costs exactly one channel

recipes.name: Antecedent and consequent
recipes.rule: Write an 8 bar period as 4 plus 4, the antecedent ending on a half cadence and the consequent ending on an authentic cadence, with both phrases opening on the same motif

recipes.name: Cadence palette
recipes.rule: End every phrase with one of the four named cadences: authentic V to I for closure, half ending on V for a question, plagal IV to I for a soft end, deceptive V to vi for a dodge, and never leave a phrase without one

recipes.name: Compressed sonata
recipes.rule: Build a 32 bar cue as 8 bars of theme A in the tonic, 8 bars of theme B in the dominant, 8 bars of development sequencing the A cell, 8 bars recapitulating both themes in the tonic, which is the shortest honest sonata form on this chip
recipes.params_text: A_bars=8; B_bars=8; development_bars=8; recap_bars=8; B_key=dominant; recap_key=tonic; total_bars=32

recipes.name: Rondo refrain loop
recipes.rule: Alternate an 8 bar refrain with two 8 bar episodes, episode one in the dominant and episode two in the relative major or minor, then close on the refrain, giving a 40 bar loop that does not read as a loop
recipes.params_text: form=ABACA; refrain_bars=8; episode_bars=8; episode_1_key=dominant; episode_2_key=relative; total_bars=40

recipes.name: Minuet figure
recipes.rule: Write 3/4 with the bass on beat 1, a chord stab on beats 2 and 3, an 8 bar binary section repeated, and the melody in quarters with a stepwise lift on beat 3
recipes.params_text: meter=3/4; bars=8; repeat=yes; bass=beat_1; stabs=beats_2_and_3; melody=quarters

recipes.name: Waltz at cue tempo
recipes.rule: Take the minuet figure to 130 to 160 bpm, put the melody in dotted rhythms in the second half of each bar, and keep the beat 2 and 3 stabs on the saw channel so the dance pulse survives the tempo

recipes.name: Function rule
recipes.rule: Label every chord tonic, pre-dominant or dominant before writing it, and forbid a pre-dominant from moving to another pre-dominant except ii to IV; this one rule removes most amateur harmonic stalls

recipes.name: Minor close, counted
recipes.rule: Take the i, iv, V7, i close and give each chord a stated number of bars, two then two then two then two, with the V7 held longest so the arrival is heard

recipes.name: Turnaround, counted
recipes.rule: Play I, vi, ii, V one bar each to close a section and reopen it, with the V on the last bar, which is the cheapest four bar engine in the score

recipes.name: Secondary dominant
recipes.rule: One bar before a target chord, play the dominant seventh of that target, resolve it on the next bar, and allow at most one secondary dominant per four bars so the colour reads as an event

recipes.name: Four bar phrase rhythm
recipes.rule: Put one chord per bar, one cadence every four bars, and never the same chord on both sides of a cadence, so the harmonic rhythm and the phrase rhythm agree

recipes.name: Power chord on two pulses
recipes.rule: Play the root on pulse1 and the fifth on pulse2 on the same grid at 50 percent duty, with no third anywhere, which is a real power chord and the only triad the chip can voice

recipes.name: Octave doubled power chord
recipes.rule: Add the octave of the root on the first VRC6 pulse at the same rhythm and lower volume, so the chord gains size without gaining a third

recipes.name: Palm mute by envelope
recipes.rule: Give every muted chord an envelope decay of three frames from volume 10 to 0 and a 50 percent gate, which is the chip's palm mute: the attack is the whole note

recipes.name: Triangle root pulse
recipes.rule: Put the root on the triangle on every eighth with an accent on beats 1 and 3, and jump the octave only on the last beat before a chord change, so the bass drives without competing with the riff

recipes.name: Rock drum kit
recipes.rule: Build the kit as DPCM kick on beats 1 and 3, noise snare on 2 and 4, and noise hat on every eighth, with the hat rate high enough to sit above the riff

recipes.name: Minor pentatonic riff
recipes.rule: Write the riff from 1, b3, 4, 5, b7 only, in a two bar cell, with the root on the beat and the highest scale tone on the last beat of the cell

recipes.name: Dorian chorus
recipes.rule: Keep the riff minor but raise the sixth, so the major chord on the fourth degree is available, and use that chord as the chorus arrival

recipes.name: Gallop rhythm
recipes.rule: Play eighth then two sixteenths, repeated every beat, on muted dyads, which is the gallop and the cheapest way to make a two bar cell sound fast

recipes.name: Half time riff
recipes.rule: Halve the riff's note values to quarters, keep the hat in eighths and the snare on 2 and 4, so the same riff reads as heavy instead of fast, which is the contrast the boss cue needs

recipes.name: Bend into the blue note
recipes.rule: Use the sweep unit with the negate flag to glide up a semitone onto the flat third and back over a quarter note, so the blue note arrives by bend rather than by a new attack

recipes.name: Verse and chorus riffs
recipes.rule: Write a verse riff on the tonic and a chorus riff transposed up a fourth with the octave doubled, three sections maximum, and loop the pair four times for a 32 bar cue

recipes.name: Ending tag
recipes.rule: End with a held power chord, a noise crash and a triangle root, held for two bars, with the mute released, which is the rock full stop

recipes.name: Tremolo by channel alternation
recipes.rule: Play one pitch at 16th rate and alternate the note between pulse1 and pulse2 on every attack, so the ear hears one continuous attack train with an accent pattern and no gap

recipes.name: Blast picking
recipes.rule: Take MET-01 to 32nd rate with a two frame decay on every attack, which is palm muted tremolo and reads as the machine gun figure rather than as a note

recipes.name: Double bass drum feel
recipes.rule: Put the DPCM kick on every 16th with the accent on alternate strokes, keep the noise snare on 2 and 4, and never leave a gap, which is what a double pedal does

recipes.name: Diminished riff on the raised seventh
recipes.rule: Build the riff from the diminished triad on the raised seventh and its tritone, one channel per note, and resolve it up a semitone to the tonic

recipes.name: Phrygian flat second riff
recipes.rule: Write the riff with the flat second next to the root as its signature move, over a i to bII vamp, and let the semitone be the riff rather than an ornament

recipes.name: Harmonic minor leap
recipes.rule: End a two bar cell with the augmented second as an upward leap from the flat sixth to the raised seventh, then resolve the seventh up to the tonic on the next strong beat

recipes.name: Neoclassical lead over V7
recipes.rule: Put the harmonic minor run in sixteenths over the dominant seventh rather than over the tonic, because the raised seventh belongs to the dominant and clashes on the tonic

recipes.name: Tritone stab
recipes.rule: Hit root and flat fifth on the two pulses as a one beat stab with a four frame decay, on beat 4 before a section change, and never twice in the same bar

recipes.name: Unison hit ending
recipes.rule: End with three unison hits on one pitch, separated by rests, then a DPCM crash and one beat of silence, so the cue stops rather than fades

recipes.name: Low register weight
recipes.rule: Keep the riff in the lowest usable pulse octave and double its root on the triangle, because the mixer sums the triangle on top of the pulses and that doubling is the only way to add weight without spending a melodic voice

recipes.name: Hook inside four bars
recipes.rule: State the hook completely inside the first 4 bars, which is 6.9 s at 104 bpm in 3/4 and 5.3 s at 180 bpm in 4/4, because average recognition is about 5 s and the fastest is 2.3 to 2.6 s

recipes.name: Identifiable from two bars
recipes.rule: Make the identifying feature audible inside the first 2 bars, because contour memory forms within 5 s and the fastest recognitions land at 2.3 to 2.6 s

recipes.name: No intro before the hook
recipes.rule: Start with the hook's own rhythmic cell in bar 1 and put any build up inside the hook; the studied stage theme opens with the figure that becomes its first half

recipes.name: Hook note budget
recipes.rule: Keep the hook between 8 and 18 notes over 2 to 4 bars, which follows from the measured 0.89 beats per note of the studied themes

recipes.name: Hook inside an octave
recipes.rule: Keep the hook within 12 semitones even when the whole cue is wider, because the measured narrow melodies are the ones that behave as riffs

recipes.name: One leap only
recipes.rule: Allow at most one interval larger than a perfect fourth in the hook, always at the same metric position, so the leap itself becomes the signature

recipes.name: Diatonic floor
recipes.rule: Keep at least 80 percent of hook notes in the key, which is the bottom of the measured 80 to 95 percent band

recipes.name: Chord tone band
recipes.rule: Land 60 to 85 percent of hook notes on chord tones, so the strong beats belong to the harmony and the weak beats carry the colour

recipes.name: Rhythm first
recipes.rule: Write the rhythmic cell before the pitches: drums alone reach 60.7 percent recognition and bass alone 54.7 percent, so rhythm carries identity without a melody

recipes.name: One predictable syncopation
recipes.rule: Put exactly one syncopation or one rest in the cell and repeat it at the same place every statement; the studied themes are tagged loose or punchy syncopation, never freely syncopated

recipes.name: Arch contour
recipes.rule: Shape the phrase as a rise to a peak near its middle then a fall back, the shape used by the studied first stage theme

recipes.name: Rise then leap down
recipes.rule: After the rise, leave the phrase with one fall, which pairs with a march or heroic cue and stays audible inside a wide range

recipes.name: Pedal then step
recipes.rule: Repeat one pitch then move by step, the design behind the measured narrow melodies that earn identity from rhythm against rich harmony

recipes.name: Repeated note anchor
recipes.rule: Anchor the hook on a repeated note so the rhythm is audible with no pitch travel; the measured narrow melodies pair an 8 to 15 semitone range with 0.88 to 0.89 beats per note

recipes.name: Exact repeat cap
recipes.rule: Repeat a phrase exactly no more than twice in a row and make the third statement carry an operation, because varied repetition outweighs literal repetition 2.7 to 1 at one measure distance

recipes.name: Sequence on the third statement
recipes.rule: Transpose the whole cell by a fixed interval for the third statement, the operation described as ubiquitous in the repertoire and cheap for early sound drivers

recipes.name: Rhythm variation once per eight bars
recipes.rule: Keep the pitches and change the rhythm or the accent once per 8 bar phrase, so the phrase reads as the same idea twice

recipes.name: Changed ending every second phrase
recipes.rule: Rewrite the last 2 notes or the cadence on every second statement, including a deceptive cadence into the relative minor, and keep the new ending loopable

recipes.name: Sixteen bar loop with an eight bar B
recipes.rule: Build the loop as 16 bars with an 8 or 16 bar B section; 16 bars is the measured workhorse loop and the wide melodies span 64 to 160 beats

recipes.name: Antecedent and consequent
recipes.rule: End the first 4 bar phrase open on the dominant and close the answering phrase with an authentic cadence, joining the melody in chords at the close as the studied theme does

recipes.name: Call and response, never doubling
recipes.rule: Give the answering voice its own path: take turns, chase a beat apart and cross registers instead of doubling the lead

recipes.name: Declare the bass type
recipes.rule: Name the bass line as walking, pedal or ostinato before writing the melody, because the bass alone carries 54.7 percent recognition

recipes.name: Couple melody to bass
recipes.rule: Keep the melody tightly coupled to the bass motion, the property the studied themes score 91 to 96 on against a database average of 50

recipes.name: One or two chromatic notes, fixed place
recipes.rule: Put one or two notes outside the key in a 4 bar hook, always on the same beat, since the measured chromatic share runs 5 to 20 percent

recipes.name: Contrast by mode first
recipes.rule: Change section by mode or key before touching instrumentation, as the studied theme moves from the major to the parallel minor while keeping tempo and cell

recipes.name: Contrast by timbre second
recipes.rule: Spend the second contrast on duty, register or voice count: 12.5 percent thin, 25 reedy, 50 hollow, one voice dropped for 2 bars, or the lead moved an octave

recipes.name: Frame jitter on non bass voices
recipes.rule: Move one non bass voice by 1 or 2 frames at the same place in each phrase, because one frame is 16.7 ms and that is the smallest human timing unit on the chip

recipes.name: Delayed vibrato, low byte only
recipes.rule: Start a small period wobble 2 to 4 frames after the attack and write only the low period byte, because a high byte write resets the phase and pops

recipes.name: Envelope per note
recipes.rule: Give each note a volume shape from the 16 hardware levels and change it in steps of 2 or more, because a 2 step change is audible and a 1 step change is not

recipes.name: Breath rest and pre change fill
recipes.rule: Rest one eighth note at the end of every 4 bar phrase on the melody voice and play a one bar noise fill before each section change, landing on the beat
